```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE) 
``` 

```{r import-data}
# Load packages
library(tidyverse)
library(caret)
library(e1071)
library(factoextra)

# 1. Create the data folder if it doesn't exist
if (!dir.exists("../data")) dir.create("../data")

# 2. Download the dataset directly to your computer first
data_url <- "https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/parkinsons/parkinsons.data"
dest_file <- "../data/parkinsons.csv"

if (!file.exists(dest_file)) {
  download.file(url = data_url, destfile = dest_file, mode = "wb")
}

# 3. Read the safely downloaded local file
parkinsons <- read_csv(dest_file)

# 4. Clean data: remove the patient 'name' column and factor the 'status' target (0 = Healthy, 1 = Parkinson's)
pk_clean <- parkinsons %>%
  select(-name) %>%
  mutate(status = factor(status, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("Healthy", "Parkinsons")))

# Verify cleaning
sum(is.na(pk_clean)) 
``` 
```{r eda}
# Class distribution plot
ggplot(pk_clean, aes(x = status, fill = status)) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Healthy vs Parkinson's Patients", x = "Diagnosis", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()

# Principal Component Analysis (PCA)
# We exclude the 'status' column (which is our target variable) and scale the numeric features
pca_res <- prcomp(pk_clean %>% select(-status), scale. = TRUE)

# Visualize PCA
fviz_pca_ind(pca_res,
             geom.ind = "point", 
             col.ind = pk_clean$status, 
             palette = c("#00AFBB", "#FC4E07"),
             addEllipses = TRUE, 
             legend.title = "Diagnosis",
             title = "PCA of Voice Acoustic Features") 
```
